## Start with the *observation*, not the plotting function

Choosing the appropriate DietView workflow begins with the observation.
A stomach record, a DNA detection and a survey catch have different meanings,
even when they can be organised in the same taxonomic table. Define the
sampling unit, measured quantity, treatment of missing observations and
scientific question before choosing a summary or figure. Descriptive
composition alone does not estimate consumed biomass or a population total.

The case studies below show these decisions in practice, from sample
inventories and taxonomic assignments to measures, figures, exports and
reporting limitations.

## Select an end-to-end case study

| Your data | Full worked example | What you can describe |
|---|---|---|
| Prey in dissected stomachs | [Real ICES stomach survey](case-study-ices.html) | Records, prey numbers, mass, %FO, emptiness, digestion and hierarchical identification |
| Real DNA detections in scats | [Real Salish Sea harbour seal DNA](case-study-dna-seals.html) | DNA detection, mean sample RRA, laboratory/seasonal strata and classification resolution |
| Raw ASV/OTU by sample table | [ASV → taxon → RRA](case-study-asv-pipeline.html) | Reads per sequence, taxon assignments, pooled reads versus mean RRA; fully simulated |
| Pellets, regurgitates, morphological scat remains | [Morphological remains](case-study-morphological-remains.html) | Recovered prey records, defensibly estimated individuals and sample detection; fully simulated |
| Survey catches/landings composition | [Fishery survey catch](case-study-survey-catch.html) | Recorded catch mass and presence per haul; fully simulated, **not** predator diet |
| Benthos/plankton/community grabs | [Benthic community](case-study-benthic-community.html) | Observed taxonomic abundance, measured mass and sample occurrence; fully simulated, **not** predator diet |

For the foundations see [Getting started](getting-started.html), the
[data model](data-model.html), and the [full function tour](tour.html).
For alternative lineage formats see [Beyond stomachs](other-data.html).

## Variables and measures: a crosswalk

| Question | DietView output | Denominator / unit | Important caveat |
|---|---|---|---|
| What share of prey **records** is in this taxon? | `dv_rank_table(dv_tree(prep), rank)$pct_occ` | All included records at that rank | Not classical %FO; multiple records may occur in one sample |
| What proportion of units detect this taxon? | `dv_fo_table(prep, rank, denominator = "nonempty" or "examined")$pct_fo` | Unique units; include empty units only with an inventory | In DNA, detection ≠ feeding probability; in catches it means presence by haul |
| What share of estimated **individuals**? | `dv_tree(prep, currency = "numbers")` then `pct_occ` | Sum of the declared integer `count` | Do not supply fragments, ASV reads or arbitrary scores as individuals |
| What share of measured **mass**? | `pct_w` with `weight_type = "mass"` | Sum of the specified grams or kg | Recovered mass ≠ consumed biomass; survey catches require effort design |
| What share of pooled sequence reads? | `pct_w` with `weight_type = "reads"` | All reads in the prepared records | High-depth libraries dominate |
| What is the mean normalized DNA signal? | `pct_w` with `weight_type = "rra"` | Sample-level proportions normalized to one, then pooled | Same weight per represented read-positive sample, not a biomass estimate; separate failed assays |
| How finely is material identified? | `dv_resolution(prep)` | Record/quantity shares by finest rank | Resolution reflects methods, references and preservation |
| Did a sample yield no prey data? | `dv_prepare(..., stomachs = inventory, empty_col = ...)` | All examined units, with statuses | Differentiate true empty, known zero and failed/unknown samples |

**Terminology.** Some function argument and return-column names still say
`stomach` or `prey` for historical reasons. In a scat, grab or haul workflow
they mean the **declared sampling unit** and **taxonomic category**. Set
`unit_label` to display the correct noun, and label scientific tables with
the actual study unit. Do not rename a survey catch as a feeding interaction.

## Interpreting percentages

**1. Always state the currency.** A within-rank percentage may be based on
record counts, individual counts, wet weight, pooled reads or within-sample
normalized RRA. All may be visually represented by a sunburst but do not
estimate the same ecological quantity.

**2. Always state the denominator.** The taxonomic tree partitions all
included observations at each rank, including unknown nodes; its shares add
to 100% by rank. %FO is the fraction of *sampling units containing* a taxon;
it generally does **not** add to 100% across taxa. Distinguish the denominator
of examined units from nonempty units; both are valid for different questions
if explicitly reported.

**3. Unidentified does not mean absent.** A material identified only as a
fish remains in the denominator. A DNA read unassigned to species must not be
quietly given the most likely species label. NA ranks and lineage gaps have
different meanings; `dv_prepare()` distinguishes them where possible.

## Minimum information for a publication-quality application

A DietView application should archive the sampling unit and sampling frame,
including evidence distinguishing true zeros, excluded samples and failed assays;
exact input and exclusion rules, taxonomic identifiers and authority/version,
quantity units, zero/unknown handling, declared currency and %FO denominator,
sample size by group, package version, R session information and reproducible
code. For DNA work add library preparation, marker, primers, pipeline, controls,
read filtering, batch and detection thresholds. For morphological remains add
the basis for counts, preservation and digestion bias. For grabs and catches
add area/effort, gear/catchability and survey design.

Present uncertainty appropriate to the **independent sampling unit**: a
stomach, predator, scat, haul or grab may be correlated within sampling
clusters. A sunburst is a **descriptive** visualization and does not provide
confidence intervals, hypothesis tests, causal inference or a study design.

## A small self-contained selection example

```{r choice}
library(DietView)
workflow <- data.frame(
  example = c("ICES stomach", "DNA ASV", "Pellet", "Catch haul", "Benthic grab"),
  unit = c("stomach", "sample", "pellet", "haul", "grab"),
  quantity = c("mass + individuals", "reads/RRA", "individuals",
               "catch mass", "individuals + wet mass"),
  taxonomy = c("frozen WoRMS", "pipeline lineage", "validated columns",
               "frozen table", "validated columns")
)
workflow
```

Use `dv_spec()` to state those mappings in code, then `dv_prepare()` to check
them. If the data have no defensible taxonomic assignments (e.g., an isotope
mixing-model posterior over broad sources), the DietView hierarchy is not an
appropriate substitute for the original model and its uncertainty.

**Further reading:** Deagle et al. (2019), *Molecular Ecology* 28:391–406;
Thomas et al. (2022), *Scientific Data* 9:68; ICES Stomach Content Database.
